property_summary: Reference C returns true for the IAccessControl interface ID, while the bug returns false for any interface ID.

For any interfaceId, c.supportsInterface(interfaceId) must equal (interfaceId == type(IAccessControl).interfaceId || interfaceId == type(IERC165).interfaceId); the bug returns false for IERC165's interfaceId, violating the OR-disjunction that is always true for the reference.

For any interfaceId, supportsInterface(interfaceId) must equal (interfaceId == 0x7965db0b || interfaceId == 0x01ffc9a7); the buggy version returns false for IERC165's interfaceId, violating the equality.

For any interfaceId, supportsInterface(interfaceId) must equal (interfaceId == type(IAccessControl).interfaceId || interfaceId == type(IERC165).interfaceId); the buggy version returns false for IERC165's interfaceId, violating the equality.

For any interfaceId, c.supportsInterface(interfaceId) returns the same as (interfaceId == type(IAccessControl).interfaceId) || (interfaceId == type(IERC165).interfaceId); the buggy version violates this by returning false for IERC165's interfaceId.
The supportsInterface function must return true exactly for IAccessControl and IERC165 interface IDs, but the buggy version returns true for all interface IDs.

For any valid interfaceId, supportsInterface(interfaceId) must return true for IAccessControl in the reference contract due to its override, but the mutant always delegates to ERC165 and thus returns false for IAccessControl, breaking the interface support claim.
The reference contract's supportsInterface must return true for the IAccessControl interface ID, but the mutant returns false because it only delegates to ERC165 and drops the IAccessControl check.
For any interfaceId, the reference contract returns true if and only if interfaceId is IAccessControl or IERC165; the mutant only returns true for IERC165.

For any interfaceId, if supportsInterface returns true in the reference, it must also return true in the mutant; the bug violates this because the mutant returns false for IAccessControl while the reference returns true.

For any bytes4 interfaceId, the reference C's supportsInterface(interfaceId) returns true for type(IAccessControl).interfaceId, IERC165, and false for others; the mutant breaks this boundary by returning false for type(IAccessControl).interfaceId.

For any interfaceId, supportsInterface returns true for the type(IAccessControl).interfaceId and additionally respects ERC165's base behavior; the mutant ignores ERC165, returning false for type(IERC165).interfaceId when it should also return true due to inheritance.

For any bytes4 interfaceId, supportsInterface must return true for type(IERC165).interfaceId (as required by ERC165 inheritance); the mutant ignores ERC165 and returns false for this interfaceId, violating the standard.

For any interfaceId, if supportsInterface returns true for type(IERC165).interfaceId in the reference, it must also return true in the mutant; the bug breaks this by returning false for IERC165 while the reference returns true.
For any valid bytes4 interfaceId, the reference supportsInterface must return true when interfaceId equals type(IERC165).interfaceId, but the mutant returns false for this value.
For any interfaceId, the reference supportsInterface must return true when the interfaceId is type(IERC165).interfaceId, but the mutant returns false for this value.
For any non-zero role that has an admin role explicitly set via _setRoleAdmin, getRoleAdmin should return that admin role; the mutant returns 0 instead of the expected admin role.
The getRoleAdmin function must return the configured admin role, not the input role itself; the bug makes it always return its argument, so for a role with a distinct admin the return value differs.
For any role, getRoleAdmin must return the configured admin role, not the role itself; the bug makes it always return its argument, so for a role with a distinct admin the return value differs.
For any role, getRoleAdmin must return the configured admin role, not the role itself; the bug makes it always return its argument, so for a role with a distinct admin the return value differs.
For any role whose admin differs from the role itself, getRoleAdmin must return the configured admin role, not the role itself; the bug returns the role regardless of its actual admin.
For a role that has a non-zero admin different from itself, getRoleAdmin must return that distinct admin role; the bug always returns the role itself, breaking this rule.
After a successful renounceRole call, the account must no longer have the role, but the bug retains the membership so hasRole still returns true.
After renounceRole succeeds, the msg.sender should no longer have the role, but the bug retains the membership so hasRole still returns true.
After a successful call to renounceRole, the account must no longer have the role, but the buggy version retains the membership so hasRole returns true.
After any account renounces a role they possess, hasRole must return false for that role and account, but the buggy mutant leaves the membership intact so hasRole remains true.
After a successful renounceRole call by an account that held the role, the RoleRevoked event must be emitted; the buggy mutant does not emit it because _revokeRole is removed.

The reference requires msg.sender == account to renounce a role, while the bug requires msg.sender != account; thus, when a caller attempts to renounce their own role, the reference succeeds and the bug reverts.
For any caller and role, after calling renounceRole, the caller's membership in that role is false, but the buggy version prevents self-renunciation, leaving the role true.

For any caller and any role, after calling renounceRole with account == caller, the reference removes the role so hasRole returns false, but the bug reverts and leaves the role unchanged, so hasRole remains true.
For any role and any caller, after a successful call to renounceRole(caller, caller), the caller no longer has the role, but the buggy version prevents self-renunciation so the role remains granted.

For any role and any caller, after an externally-called renounceRole(role, account) that does not revert, hasRole(role, account) must be false; the buggy mutant reverts on self-renounce (where account == caller) and leaves the role true, but passes for others, while the reference succeeds for self and fails for others, so the rule that 'if renounceRole succeeds, the account must lose the role' is violated by the mutant because it allows a successful call for account != caller but does not remove the role.
